title: Tenali and the Royal Portrait

keywords: tenali and the painting of the king
full_text:
King Krishnadevaraya, though a handsome and charismatic monarch, had a slight physical blemish: he had lost the sight in his left eye during a youthful battle, leaving a distinct scar across that side of his face.
Wishing to leave a magnificent portrait for posterity, the King invited three celebrated painters to capture his likeness on canvas.

The first artist, an eager flatterer, painted the King with two perfectly clear, radiant eyes, erasing the battle scar entirely.
The King looked at the painting and frowned:
'Thou art a liar! This is not my face; thou hast flattered me with a false mask, dishonoring the wound I received defending our empire!'
The painter was dismissed in disgrace.

The second artist, determined to be strictly realistic, painted the King with his scarred, blind left eye prominently enlarged, red and weeping.
The King was deeply offended:
'Thou hast no aesthetic sense or respect! Thou hast turned an imperial portrait into a gruesome medical illustration!'
He, too, was sent away.

The King, exasperated, turned to Tenali Raman:
'Tenali, thou art a man of discernment. Canst thou find an artist who can depict me with both truth and majesty?'

Tenali took up the brushes himself: 'Maharaj, allow me to paint your portrait.'
Tenali set up an easel, asked the King to pose, and worked for three days.

When the portrait was unveiled before the full court, a collective gasp of admiration filled the hall.
Tenali had painted King Krishnadevaraya on horseback in an exquisite profile view, drawing a golden bow with focused concentration, aiming an arrow at a flying deer.
His right profile was turned toward the viewer, showing his healthy, commanding right eye narrowed in marksman precision, while his scarred left eye was naturally turned away toward the target!

The portrait was historically accurate, dignified, heroic, and completely free of both flattery and ugliness!

King Krishnadevaraya was moved to tears by Tenali’s exquisite tact and artistic brilliance:
'Tenali, thou hast captured my true spirit as a warrior-king without falsifying my wound or insulting my dignity!'
The King embraced Tenali, awarded him five hundred gold coins and a royal robe of honor, demonstrating that true tact balances truth with grace.
moral: Tactful honesty that preserves dignity while telling truth is the highest art of courtly service.
